scope: make sanitize: generated Goose program, Goose runtime and native adapter under ASan/UBSan, with a sensitive negative control

coverage.sqlite_linked_dynamically: NOT instrumented (system library; documented limit of docs/results/audit-2026-11-04.json)

generated_translation_unit.method: compile the generated C to an object with scripts/sanitizer-cc.sh -c, then nm | grep -c

sanitize_binaries.note: clang statically links its ASan/UBSan runtime, so its symbol counts are much higher than gcc's dynamic libasan.so.8/libubsan.so.1

native_adapter_library.note: distinct cache keys per compiler wrapper, so no stale non-sanitized native library is reused

negative_control.fault: ffi::bytes reads 64 bytes from a 16-byte heap buffer; ffi trusts the pointer and length, so no Goose bounds check intervenes

gcc.stack: main_g -> gs_ffi_bytes -> gs_bld_append in the generated sanitize_fault.c

clang.stack: main_g -> gs_ffi_bytes -> gs_bld_append in the generated sanitize_fault.c

negative_control.gate: scripts/sanitize-control.py fails make sanitize unless the run aborts with AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow

sensitivity_control.purpose: prove the control is sensitive: the same fault must be silent without instrumentation
sensitivity_control.uninstrumented_build: goose build tests/sanitize_fault.goose --cc <plain wrapper linking tests/sanitize_fault.c> --standalone
sensitivity_control.conclusion: instrumented run aborts, uninstrumented run is silent, so the control detects the instrumentation rather than a crash that would happen anyway

make check.note: includes goose format --check over tests, which covers tests/sanitize_fault.goose

make test-native CC=gcc.note: run in two bounded invocations because the recovery step alone takes about 277s

make test-native CC=clang.note: run in two bounded invocations for the same reason

scripts/test-wal-engine.py.note: pinned instrumented SQLite engine; unchanged by this work

limitations: The dynamically linked system SQLite 3.54.1 is not instrumented; only the adapter, runtime and generated program are.

The negative control injects its fault through ffi::bytes, which is documented to trust the caller's pointer and length. It proves the generated translation unit is instrumented and sensitive; it is not a claim that the public sqlite API has a memory bug.
Goose's own bounds, overflow and division checks stop most natural faults before the sanitizer sees them, which is why the control uses an unchecked ffi path rather than an out-of-range Goose index.
The scoped ThreadSanitizer cold-start limitation in docs/validation.md is unchanged and not addressed here.
Local shared-host results are not CI thresholds, universal rankings or a SOTA claim.
